clue.text: Raised spirits with this description of Oxford

definitions.meaning: a drink with a slug of brandy or rum added to it has been fortified, and that pick-me-up is what raises the spirits
an Oxford is a style of shoe fastened with laces

explanation.surface: A toast to the university town that lifts everyone's mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Oxford looks like the university city, but here it is a kind of shoe.
explanation.definitionFit: A drink spiked with spirits is said to be fortified that way, and Oxford shoes are tied with laces.

clue.text: What successful people never do furiously in play

parts.note: the winners keep their eyes forward and never turn to review the past
acting furiously is acting with rage, in wrath

explanation.surface: A tip for winners about never acting in rage on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The play is John Osborne's 1956 drama about the 'angry young man' Jimmy Porter.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the title of a famous stage drama by John Osborne.

clue.text: American style of cooking, taking about a month, in short

parts.note: CA is short for circa, Latin for around
JUN is the usual abbreviation for June

explanation.surface: A summary of a month-long course in an American regional cuisine.
explanation.definitionFit: Louisiana's Acadian-descended people gave their name to a spicy regional cuisine.

clue.text: Require another person to take the record, as a rule

definitions.text: Require another person to take the record, as a rule

parts.words: Require another person to take the record, as a rule
parts.note: the phrase describes speaking a letter for a secretary to write down, and also laying down rules that others must follow

explanation.walkthrough: The clue blends two senses: speaking words for someone to write down, and imposing rules on others.
explanation.definitionFit: To speak aloud for transcription, and to command authoritatively, are both senses of this verb.

clue.text: Mouthpiece for launch of romantic hits?

definitions.meaning: the double curve of the upper lip is named for an archer's weapon
the god of love shoots his arrows from his own weapon

explanation.surface: Advice on how to kick off a set of love songs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hits' suggests chart songs, but they are arrow strikes from the god of love.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper lip's curved outline and the Roman love god's archery weapon share the name.

clue.text: First thing needed by computer following modern style

definitions.text: First thing needed by computer following modern style

indicators.note: the next piece comes after the opening letter in the answer
the opening letter is what the word computer starts with

parts.note: hip means fashionable, up to date

explanation.surface: Advice on what a computer needs first if it is to be up to date.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: a processor is the first thing a computer needs.
explanation.definitionFit: A silicon microprocessor is the essential component of any computer.

clue.text: Quiet about his Conservative past, not on record

parts.note: P is piano, the musical direction for softly
RE means concerning, on the subject of
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A Tory politician keeps silent about his own unrecorded history.
explanation.definitionFit: The era before written history is, by definition, unrecorded time.

clue.text: Play round with defence in practice

parts.note: DEF is a common abbreviation for defence
to play a part is to act
a round shape is the letter O

explanation.surface: A sports pundit says a practice game has shifted round the defence.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means existing in reality, whether or not officially sanctioned.

clue.text: Ask to take part in baseball game, for a start

parts.note: to beg is to ask earnestly
an inning is one division of a baseball game

explanation.surface: A newcomer pleads to join a game of baseball.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening or commencement is a start.

clue.text: Travelling with personal pack, going by air from Australia

definitions.meaning: in Australian slang a swagman carrying his bundle of belongings is said to be doing this
an air is a tune, and this is Australia's best-known folk song

explanation.surface: A backpacker flies out of Australia with their luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Going by air' suggests a flight, but the air is a tune.
explanation.definitionFit: Australian slang for tramping with a swag gave its name to the country's famous folk song.

clue.text: Dispassionate locum's case

definitions.meaning: locum is the Latin accusative of locus, and the accusative is called the ... case in English grammar

explanation.surface: A stand-in doctor's patient file is handled without emotion.
explanation.walkthrough: Locum looks like a stand-in doctor, but it is a Latin word form.
explanation.definitionFit: Being impartial means being unbiased, and grammar's accusative is also named for objects of verbs.

clue.text: Bad atmosphere a learner associated with a musical form

parts.note: a fug is a stuffy, smoky room atmosphere
L is for learner, as on British L-plates

explanation.surface: A music student endures a stuffy practice room.
explanation.definitionFit: This adjective describes the fugue, a contrapuntal composition.

clue.text: A pretentious type rejected one unnaturally small tree

indicators.note: rejected is read as thrown back, so the words before it run in reverse

parts.note: a snob is a pretentious person
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A snob has turned down a stunted little tree.
explanation.definitionFit: This Japanese art form deliberately keeps trees dwarfed in pots.

clue.text: Visual aid mounted on bridge

parts.note: the bridge is that of the nose, where a pair of clip-on spectacles perches without arms

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests a structure over a river or a ship's bridge, but it is the bridge of the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: These old-style spectacles grip the nose with a spring and have no earpieces.

clue.text: On which king's laid down with resignation

definitions.text: On which king's laid down with resignation

parts.words: On which king's laid down with resignation
parts.note: a monarch abdicating suggests itself, but this is a game piece toppled when a player resigns

explanation.walkthrough: A chess player concedes by laying their king on its side.
explanation.definitionFit: The checkered playing board is where a defeated player tips over the king.

clue.text: It went to one's head, being badly beaten in this

definitions.meaning: a three-cornered hat was worn on the head
the idiom knocked into a three-cornered hat means thoroughly defeated

explanation.surface: Success went to someone's head, until a crushing defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Went to one's head' suggests conceit or drink, but it is just headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A tricorn hat sat on the head, and an idiom about it means outclassed.

clue.text: What causes clot to misuse a gun (a Colt)?

indicators.note: misuse means the letters are badly handled and rearranged

explanation.surface: A clot of a man mishandles a Colt revolver.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clot' looks like a dimwit wielding a gun, but it is a blood clot.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that thickens blood or liquid into a clot is so named.

clue.text: Source of bulb one's repeatedly lit outside

indicators.note: outside means the doubled word goes around the numeral
repeatedly means the word for lit is used twice over

parts.note: a lit lamp is on
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A light bulb keeps being switched on outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bulb' suggests a light, but it is a plant bulb.
explanation.definitionFit: This vegetable is itself a bulb, the source of bulbs for planting.

clue.text: I had a garden tool shortened for major potato producer

parts.note: I'D is the contraction of I had

indicators.note: shortened means the tool's word loses its last letter

parts.note: a hoe is a weeding tool

explanation.surface: A gardener's hoe was cut down while working potato fields.
explanation.definitionFit: This northwestern US state is famous for growing potatoes.

clue.text: Loves the lines put in for title role

indicators.note: put in means the middle pieces go inside the two zeros

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O, so two loves are OO
L is an abbreviation for line, so LL for lines

explanation.surface: An actor puts in the lines for the starring part.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's tragedy is named for its Moorish general, the lead part.

clue.text: Plan way to desert a wonderful person

parts.note: ST is street, a way
to rat is to desert one's side
a gem is someone treasured

explanation.surface: A scheme to abandon a lovely person.
explanation.definitionFit: A cunning scheme or ruse.

clue.text: Classic building to shake violently

indicators.note: violently signals that the words are thrown about into a new order

explanation.surface: A classic old building is shaken badly.
explanation.walkthrough: The Oaks, at Epsom, is one of the five British horse-racing Classics.
explanation.definitionFit: This Epsom race for fillies is one of English flat racing's five Classics.

clue.text: An American friend, by custom, docked in Arab port

parts.note: bud is American slang for buddy

indicators.note: docked means the word for custom loses its tail

parts.note: a habit is a custom

explanation.surface: An American pal follows tradition and docks at an Arab harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Docked' looks like a ship mooring, but it means cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: The UAE's capital is a port on the Persian Gulf.

clue.text: Holiday one must have or break, here?

indicators.note: must have tells us the word for break contains the other piece

parts.note: a rest is a break

explanation.surface: A holiday maker must choose whether to stay or break off here.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Holiday one' means a holiday spot; 'here?' is a closing flourish.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaside or ski destination is where holidaymakers go.

clue.text: No use looking inside for this bird

indicators.note: inside signals the answer lies within the run of words

explanation.surface: It's pointless looking inside for this bird.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old name for the blackbird, or the water ouzel.

clue.text: Navigable launch

definitions.meaning: ... water is clear for ships to pass
to launch a business is to start it up

explanation.definitionFit: Clear water is passable, and starting an exhibition is inaugurating it.

clue.text: King having trouble — knights went after it

parts.note: GR is Georgius Rex, King George
to ail is to trouble

explanation.surface: An ailing king sends his knights on a quest.
explanation.walkthrough: The Arthurian knights' quest was for the holy cup.
explanation.definitionFit: The Holy cup was the quest of the Round Table knights.

clue.text: Evaluation of artist one's received in alarm

indicators.note: received in means the pieces are taken inside the word for alarm

parts.note: to appal is to alarm
RA is a Royal Academician
I'S is one is, I being the Roman one

explanation.surface: An artist is alarmed to receive a critical review.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment or valuation.

clue.text: With retired staff, study is gone over again

parts.note: a rod is a staff
a den is a study

explanation.surface: Retired staff find their old study has been revisited.
explanation.definitionFit: Trodden again means walked over again.

clue.text: Saucy dance girl almost repeated

indicators.note: almost means the last letter is lost
repeated means the girl's name is written twice

parts.note: Sal is a girl's name, short for Sally

explanation.surface: A cheeky girl dances almost the same step twice.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin dance shares its name with a spicy tomato sauce.
